key_insight: OmniShotCut reframes shot boundary detection as a structured relational prediction problem and introduces a shot‑query Transformer that jointly reasons about shot boundaries and inter-shot relations, producing more interpretable, sensitive, and robust boundary detections.
problem_solved: Existing SBD methods give non‑interpretable boundary predictions, miss subtle but harmful discontinuities, and rely on noisy, low‑diversity annotations and outdated benchmarks—limiting downstream video understanding tasks and reliable evaluation.
method: Shot‑Query Transformer: use learnable shot queries to simultaneously predict shot boundaries and relational links between frames/shots via cross‑attention.
Structured relational prediction: model pairwise and higher‑order relationships to disambiguate gradual, abrupt, and complex transitions and yield interpretable boundary scores.
Cleaner supervision & evaluation: incorporate higher‑quality annotations and updated benchmark protocols to improve training robustness and comparative evaluation.
impact: Delivers more reliable and interpretable shot segmentation for video pipelines, improving preprocessing for tasks like video retrieval, summarization, and downstream temporal understanding while offering stronger benchmarks for future SBD research.
visual_elements: Schematic of the Shot‑Query Transformer: timeline of frames with shot queries attending to frame regions (attention heatmaps) and emitting boundary + relation outputs.
Before/after timeline: example video timeline showing original noisy boundaries vs. OmniShotCut's refined, interpretable boundaries with labels (abrupt, gradual, continuity).
Attention/relational heatmap: matrix visualizing predicted inter‑frame/shot affinities that explain why a boundary was placed.
Performance comparison chart: precision/recall or F1 bars showing robustness on subtle transitions and under noisy labels (qualitative + quantitative callouts).
paper_title: OmniShotCut: Holistic Relational Shot Boundary Detection with Shot-Query Transformer
paper_authors: Boyang Wang, Guangyi Xu, Zhipeng Tang, Jiahui Zhang, Zezhou Cheng
